content.text:
GitHub Actions secrets live on **GitHub**, not in Cursor. The plugin only tells the workflow to read names like `${{ secrets.FOO }}` — you still add the values in the repo settings.

This repo is [AminMortezaie/kuchup](https://github.com/AminMortezaie/kuchup). Current CI in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` does not use any secrets; you only need them once a deploy (or other) workflow references them.

## GitHub website (easiest)

1. Open **[Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions](https://github.com/AminMortezaie/kuchup/settings/secrets/actions)**  
   (Repo → **Settings** → **Secrets and variables** → **Actions**. You need admin access.)
2. Click **New repository secret**.
3. **Name** must match the workflow exactly (case-sensitive), e.g. `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`.
4. Paste the **Value**. Save.

To change a secret later: same page → the secret → **Update**. You cannot read the old value; you can only replace it.

## GitHub CLI

If `gh` is installed and you’re logged in (`gh auth login`):

```bash
gh secret set SECRET_NAME --repo AminMortezaie/kuchup
```

It prompts for the value (nothing is printed). Or pipe it:

```bash
printf '%s' "$THE_VALUE" | gh secret set SECRET_NAME --repo AminMortezaie/kuchup
```

List names only (values are never shown):

```bash
gh secret list --repo AminMortezaie/kuchup
```

## Use them in a workflow

```yaml
env:
  MY_SECRET: ${{ secrets.SECRET_NAME }}
```

or:

```yaml
- name: Example
  run: ./scripts/something.sh
  env:
    AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID: ${{ secrets.AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID }}
    AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY: ${{ secrets.AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY }}
```

Secrets from forks are **not** available on `pull_request` from other people. Production deploys should run on `push` to `main` (or `workflow_dispatch`), not on untrusted PRs.

## Don’t mix this up with Cursor plugin config

| Where | What it is |
|--------|------------|
| GitHub **Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions** | Used by GitHub Actions (`${{ secrets.NAME }}`) |
| Cursor **Plugins → Configure** | Tokens for Cursor MCP/plugins only — CI cannot see these |

## This public repo

Never put real IPs, `DATABASE_URL`, SSH keys, or passwords in workflow YAML, docs, or commits. Only the secret **name** belongs in the workflow; the **value** stays in GitHub’s secret store.

If you tell me which secret names the plugin listed (or paste the workflow snippet), I can map them to the exact values you already have locally (`.env` / `aws-postgres.env`) without putting those values in git.

also we need to add github to allowed on AWS to can deploy from it on my server how to do this?

GitHub Actions runners use changing IPs, so the EC2 security group that currently allows only your laptop will block deploy. I’ll check how this repo opens SSH today and give you the exact AWS change.

You cannot add “GitHub” as a permanent allowlist in the AWS console. GitHub Actions runners get a **new public IP on every job**, and this box only allows SSH from **your laptop** today (`./scripts/aws_postgres_migrate.sh sync-sg` opens port **22** for your current IP).

Do **not** open SSH to `0.0.0.0/0`. Do **not** dump all GitHub IP ranges into the security group (there are too many for a normal SG).

**What works:** the deploy workflow itself opens port 22 for *that runner’s IP*, deploys, then closes it. You already have the AWS keys in `.env` (`AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` / `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`), and those keys can already change the security group.

The job needs something like this **before** SSH/rsync, and a matching revoke in `if: always()`:

```bash
RUNNER_IP="$(curl -fsS https://checkip.amazonaws.com | tr -d '[:space:]')"
aws ec2 authorize-security-group-ingress \
  --region eu-central-1 \
  --group-id "$SECURITY_GROUP_ID" \
  --ip-permissions "IpProtocol=tcp,FromPort=22,ToPort=22,IpRanges=[{CidrIp=${RUNNER_IP}/32,Description=github-actions-deploy}]"
```

After deploy:

```bash
aws ec2 revoke-security-group-ingress \
  --region eu-central-1 \
  --group-id "$SECURITY_GROUP_ID" \
  --ip-permissions "IpProtocol=tcp,FromPort=22,ToPort=22,IpRanges=[{CidrIp=${RUNNER_IP}/32}]"
```

`$SECURITY_GROUP_ID` comes from `aws-postgres.env` (the `AWS_POSTGRES_ENV` secret you already added). Only **port 22**. Do not open 5432 to GitHub.

If the plugin’s workflow does not already do this, the deploy job will hang or fail on SSH even with a correct `EC2_SSH_KEY`. Paste the workflow YAML (or say you want it added) and I can wire these steps in.

<timestamp>Monday, Sep 21, 2026, 2:42 PM (UTC+4)</timestamp>

so it cannot be automatically you mean?

It **can** be automatic. You just cannot do it once in the AWS console and forget it.

A GitHub Actions job can, on every deploy:

1. Read its own public IP  
2. Open SSH (port 22) for that IP on your security group  
3. Deploy  
4. Close that rule again  

You would not click anything in AWS. The keys you already put in `EC2_DEPLOY_DOTENV` are enough for that, as long as the workflow includes those steps.

What is **not** automatic is a permanent “allow GitHub” checkbox. GitHub’s IPs change every run, so AWS has nothing named GitHub to allow forever.

If you want, I can add those open-deploy-close steps to the deploy workflow so you never have to think about the security group.

# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1
# Slow panel base: tectonic binary + TeX package warm + pip.
# Tagged relocation-panel-deps:ec2 and rebuilt only when this file,
# requirements.txt, or deploy/ec2/tectonic-warm.tex change.
FROM python:3.12-slim-bookworm

ENV PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 \
    PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 \
    PANEL_DATA_DIR=/tmp/panel-data \
    PANEL_SCRAPE_ENABLED=0 \
    PANEL_COMPANY_FETCH_ENABLED=1 \
    PORT=10000

ARG TECTONIC_VERSION=0.16.9

WORKDIR /app

RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    ca-certificates \
    curl \
    && ARCH="$(dpkg --print-architecture)" \
    && case "$ARCH" in \
         amd64) TECTONIC_TARGET=x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu ;; \
         arm64) REDACTED ;; \
         *) echo "unsupported arch: $ARCH" >&2; exit 1 ;; \
       esac \
    && curl -fsSL "https://github.com/tectonic-typesetting/tectonic/releases/download/tectonic%40${TECTONIC_VERSION}/tectonic-${TECTONIC_VERSION}-${TECTONIC_TARGET}.tar.gz" \
         | tar -xz -C /usr/local/bin tectonic \
    && chmod +x /usr/local/bin/tectonic \
    && apt-get purge -y curl \
    && apt-get autoremove -y \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Warm Tectonic package cache so first production render does not download over the network.
COPY deploy/ec2/tectonic-warm.tex /tmp/tectonic-warm/warm.tex
RUN tectonic --outdir /tmp/tectonic-warm /tmp/tectonic-warm/warm.tex \
    && rm -rf /tmp/tectonic-warm

# Panel does not scrape on EC2 — skip playwright (~130MB) and browsers.
COPY requirements.txt .
RUN --mount=type=cache,id=relocation-panel-pip,target=/root/.cache/pip \
    pip install -r requirements.txt

# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1
# EC2 panel app layer (no Playwright). Tectonic/pip live in
# relocation-panel-deps:ec2 — see Dockerfile.ec2-deps.
FROM relocation-panel-deps:ec2

WORKDIR /app

COPY . .
RUN chmod +x docker-entrypoint.sh docker-entrypoint-mcp.sh

RUN mkdir -p /tmp/panel-data

EXPOSE 10000 10001

CMD ["./docker-entrypoint.sh"]

content.text:
That Tectonic step was never supposed to run on every deploy. It sat in the same image as the Python app, and EC2’s Docker cache was not keeping that layer, so any panel rebuild re-downloaded TeX.

**What changed:** Tectonic + pip now live in a tagged image `relocation-panel-deps:ec2` (`Dockerfile.ec2-deps`). The panel image is only `FROM` that plus a copy of the app.

| Change | Rebuilds Tectonic? |
|--------|-------------------|
| Python / panel code | No — app layer only |
| `requirements.txt`, Tectonic version, or warm `.tex` | Yes |
| `deploy --force` | Yes |

The **next** deploy will still run Tectonic **once** to create the deps image. After that, a normal local deploy should not show `RUN tectonic --outdir /tmp/tectonic-warm`.
